title: Personal Credit Cards: combined credit line cap across a customer's cards
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: combined credit line cap

This policy covers the Personal Credit Cards line and applies when a card application is recorded, when a card is approved and when a credit limit changes. It aggregates credit lines across all of a customer's PCB cards.

## Policy clauses

1. The customer's combined credit lines are the credit limits of all of the customer's card accounts whose status is applied, active or suspended, taken together and including the requested or new limit.
2. The combined credit lines must not exceed 75000.00 USD, or 150000.00 USD when the customer holds an active Private Client Checking account.
3. An approval or an increase that would breach the cap is limited to the remaining headroom.
4. An approval is declined when that headroom is below the tier's smallest credit limit; an increase is declined when that headroom is zero.
5. Decreases are never limited by the cap.
6. Secured card limits count toward the cap like any other line.

## Which cap applies

| Customer holds an active Private Client Checking account | Cap on combined credit lines |
|---|---|
| yes | 150000.00 USD |
| no | 75000.00 USD |

The check reads the bank's records of the customer's card accounts and checking accounts before the approval or limit change; it is decided on those records.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical customers without Private Client Checking)

- Existing lines total 70000.00 USD and a new card is being approved on a tier whose smallest limit is 1000.00 USD (a hypothetical figure). The headroom is 5000.00 USD, so the approval is limited to at most 5000.00 USD, which is not below the smallest limit.
- Existing lines total 74500.00 USD on the same hypothetical tier. The headroom is 500.00 USD, below the smallest limit, so the approval is declined.
- Existing lines total 75000.00 USD and an increase is requested. The combined lines already equal the cap, so the headroom is zero and the increase is declined.
- Combined lines that come to exactly 75000.00 USD including the new limit do not exceed the cap.

## Basis Q&A

**Q: Does a decrease on one card have to fit under the cap?**
A: No. Decreases are never limited by the cap.

**Q: Does a Secured Visa limit count?**
A: Yes. Secured card limits count toward the cap like any other line.
